RagShortTexts: The Comunos family ruled the Western Empire, and the head of the family was Galios.

Variants.Content: The Comunos family is the ruling family of the Western Empire, and the head of the family is Galios. He was originally a famous general under the late Emperor Arenicos and had great military exploits. After the assassination of the first emperor, the empire was divided. With the support of veterans and border legions, Galios proclaimed himself emperor in the west and made Lys, Jarma, his capital. The flag of the Comunos family was raised on the battlefield, not canonized by the Senate.

The Comunos family? That was the family of General Galios. He has been bleeding on the battlefield for half his life, fighting Battania and Aserai. In which battle is he not at the forefront? When the late emperor was alive, the empire could still hold together. But when the late emperor died, the talkers in the Senate wanted to establish Lucon, but we soldiers refused. Galios is a soldier, and he knows how to treat soldiers. The throne of the Western Empire was given to him by veterans like us who sacrificed our lives.

The Comunos family controls the western part of the empire, which has many mountains and few ports. It is not as rich as the south, but it is easy to defend and difficult to attack militarily. Garius is a good fighter, but running a country does not rely solely on fighting. The market in Jalma Lys has become increasingly deserted in the past two years, and the caravans have all gone south to the territory of Queen Rhagaea. When a soldier becomes an emperor, it is us who do business who suffer.

The Comunos family represents another path of the empire - the supremacy of military merit. Garius never believed in the Senate, nor did he believe in blood. He believed in the veterans who had squatted in trenches and suffered arrows with him. There were no senators in the court of the Western Empire, only generals. Some people say this is a betrayal of the imperial tradition, but if the imperial tradition was useful, the late emperor would not have been assassinated.

The roots of the Comunos family lie in the military. The people Emperor Galios trusted most were not the nobles or senators, but the old brothers who had fought with him. In the Western Empire, the words of a centurion were more effective than those of a senator. This method works well during a battle, but what happens after the battle is over? Those veterans wanted land, wanted dinars, wanted status—how much could Galios give them? If you give too little, they will rebel; if you give too much, the nobles will rebel. The Comunos family sits on the crater.

I fought with the Emperor Galios against the people of Battania. In the ambush in the woods that day, we were surrounded on three sides. The general himself rushed up with his guards and pulled us out. From that day on, I determined that this life belonged to the Comunos family. Lucon talks in the Senate, Rhagaea feeds on her dead husband, and only Galios crawls out of blood like us.

The Comunos family? It's just a fake emperor promoted by a group of soldiers. The imperial throne has never been decided by swords - it must be approved by the Senate and comply with the imperial legal system. What does Galios have? Besides knowing how to fight, what qualifications does he have to sit in that position? He didn't even know which way the Senate door opened. Sooner or later, the Western Empire was ruined by his barbaric rules of "veterans first".

The Comunos family was one of the sinners of the division of the empire. Even before the bones of the late emperor Arenicos were cold, Galios was eager to stand on his own in the west, completely ignoring the orthodoxy of the Petlos family. Queen Rhagaea is the widow of the late emperor, and Princess Ila is the blood of the late emperor - this is the center around which the empire should be united. The throne that Garius had snatched away with his sword would have to be returned with his sword sooner or later.

The Western Empire controlled by the Comunos family borders Vlandia, and we have fought more wars with them than anyone else. Galios is a tough nut, and his border legions are not easy to chew. But having said that, a regime that relies on veterans is most afraid of the veterans dying of old age. How old is Galios? How old were his centurions? Ten years later, who else in the Western Empire can fight for him?

The Comunos are the mortal enemies of us Battanians. Galios has been fighting our clan on the western border for more than ten years, burning many sacred groves and cutting down many ancient oak trees. His veterans all have Battanian blood on their hands. Now that he has become the emperor, he has turned the main force of the legion to the imperial civil war, and the pressure on our north is less. But the people of Battania will never forget this blood debt.

The relationship between the Comunos family and the Aserai is pretty good. Galios' main enemies were Battania and Vlandia, and the southern front was relatively peaceful. Caravans from the Western Empire occasionally cross the desert to do business in Guyaz, and their spending is more generous than the stingy senators from the Northern Empire. Soldiers are not good at calculating detailed accounts, which is not a bad thing for businessmen.

We northerners can understand the Comunos family’s practice of “veterans choosing the emperor.” Sturgia's Boyer is also typed, not born. Had Galios been born in the north, he would have been a good boy. It's a pity that he was born in the Empire. The people of the Empire talk about the Republic, but all they think about is bloodline and the Senate. They could not tolerate an emperor who rose to power by sword.

The Comunos family is too far away from us, separated by an entire empire. But the Khuzait respect warriors, and Galios was indeed a warrior. I heard he could cut down an entire team of Battania Raiders by himself when he was younger. Such a man, if born on the grassland, would be a good sweat king. It's a pity that he was born in the empire, where the rules are not bows and horses, but conspiracy and the Senate.

The Comunos family recruits mercenaries more generously than anyone else. Emperor Galios knew that his veterans had fewer battles to fight, so he was willing to pay for the lives of outsiders. I worked a few times in the Western Empire, and the money was given freely, unlike in Lucon, where every dinar had to be signed by three senators. But there's a downside to working for Galios - his battles are never finished.

The rise of the Comunos family represented a major break in the imperial political tradition. In the history of the empire, there were three main sources of legitimacy for the throne: Senate recognition, bloodline inheritance, and military support. Gallius was the first emperor to come to power purely relying on military support, and the legitimacy of his regime was entirely based on the loyalty of the veteran class. The advantage of this model is that it has strong cohesion in the short term, but its disadvantage is that it lacks a sustainable institutionalized inheritance mechanism. After Galios died, who was qualified to succeed him? Who will his generals obey? The Comunos family may have been just a brief culmination of imperial military power and politics, rather than the beginning of a stable dynasty.

The basis of the rule of the Comunos family was the Frontier Legion. Galios has operated on the western border for many years, turning the border guards into his own private army. There were no senators or big businessmen in his inner circle, only centurions and legion commanders. There is no doubt about the combat effectiveness of this team, but governing an empire requires more than just combat effectiveness. The administrative system of the Western Empire is still not functioning smoothly because Galios does not trust civil servants at all - he only trusts those who have shed blood with him.

The Comunos family is a purely male-dominated family. Who is the wife of Gallius? No one remembers. Who is his daughter? No one mentioned it. Women had almost no place in the power landscape of the Western Empire—there were only generals, centurions, and veterans. Queen Rhagaea at least gave women in the southern part of the empire a possibility, but in the western empire, women still had to stay at the rear.
